text: The application for approval of a vehicle type with regard to the ACPE shall be submitted by the vehicle manufacturer or by his authorized representative.
The application for type-approval shall be accompanied by the documents mentioned below in triplicate.

The vehicle manufacturer shall provide a description of the vehicle type with regard to the items mentioned in paragraph 2.2., together with a documentation package which gives access to the basic design of the ACPE and the means by which the ACPE is linked to other vehicle systems or by which the ACPE directly controls output variables.
The numbers and/or symbols identifying the vehicle type shall be specified.
The vehicle representative of the vehicle type to be approved shall be submitted to the Technical Service conducting the approval tests.
The Contracting Party shall assign an approval number to each vehicle type approved.

The first two digits of the approval number assigned to each vehicle type approved (00 for the Regulation in its initial form) shall indicate the series of amendments incorporating the most recent major technical amendments made to the Regulation at the time of issue of the approval.
The same Contracting Party shall not assign the same approval number to the same vehicle type equipped with another type of ACPE, or to another vehicle type.

The vehicle conforming to a vehicle type approved under this Regulation shall have affixed, conspicuously and in a readily accessible place specified on the approval form, an international approval mark conforming to the model described in Annex 2, consisting of the elements specified in the regulation.

While the vehicle conforms to a vehicle type approved under one or more other Regulations annexed to the Agreement, in the country which has granted approval under this Regulation, the Regulation and approval numbers and the additional symbols shall be placed in vertical columns to the right of the symbol prescribed in paragraph 4.4.1. above; however, the symbol prescribed in paragraph 4.4.1. above need not be repeated.
The approval mark shall be clearly legible and be indelible.
The approval mark shall be placed close to or on the vehicle data plate.

When an accelerator control misapplication by the driver has been detected at least when an obstacle exists in front of the vehicle when the driving direction is selected to be forward, the ACPE shall be able to limit unintended acceleration of the vehicle.

When an accelerator control misapplication by the driver has been detected at least when an obstacle exists behind the vehicle when the driving direction is selected to be rearwards, the ACPE shall be able to limit unintended acceleration of the vehicle.

The accelerator control application having a velocity of at least 400 per cent per second over a travel distance of at least 70 per cent of the total travel distance of the accelerator control, and reaching a maximum position of the accelerator control of at least 90 per cent with that velocity shall be regarded as an accelerator control misapplication in the context of the paragraph 5.1.1.

Notwithstanding paragraph 5.1.2., in the case of systems that implement force-based triggering of the ACPE, the system shall consider an accelerator control force greater than the triggering threshold as accelerator control misapplication.
In the case of systems that implement force-based triggering of the ACPE, the manufacturer shall justify the triggering threshold to the satisfaction of the Type Approval Authority.
When the vehicle is accelerated from standstill, the ACPE shall control acceleration.
If ACPE is not ready to perform an intervention 6 seconds after the initiation of the vehicle powertrain, then the ACPE shall indicate information of this status to the driver.

While the system has not been successfully initialised, when 6 seconds have elapsed after the initiation of the vehicle powertrain and ACPE is not ready to perform an intervention, the ACPE shall provide information of this status.

When the accelerator control is applied, the ACPE shall limit vehicle acceleration in order to prevent or mitigate a collision with an obstacle located between 1.0 m and 1.5 m in front of or behind the vehicle, in the vehicle path, provided: (a) Vehicle external influences allow for the required acceleration inhibition, i.e.: (i) The road is flat, horizontal and dry affording good adhesion; (ii) The weather conditions do not affect the performance of the vehicle (e.g. no storm, not below 0°C); (b) The vehicle state itself allows for the required acceleration inhibition, e.g.: (i) The tyres are in an appropriate state and properly inflated; (ii) The brakes if intended to be used are properly operational (brake temperature, pads condition etc.); (iii) There is no severe uneven load distribution; (iv) No trailer is coupled to the motor vehicle and the mass of the motor vehicle is between maximum mass and mass in running order conditions; (v) The vehicle’s powertrain management system is properly operational (c) There are no external influences affecting the physical sensing capabilities, i.e.: (i) The ambient illumination conditions are at least 1000 Lux and there is no extreme blinding of the sensors (e.g. direct blinding sunlight, highly radar-reflective environment); (ii) The target vehicle is not extreme with regard to the Radar Cross Section (RCS) or the shape/silhouette (e.g. below fifth percentile of RCS of all M1 vehicles) (iii) There are no significant weather conditions affecting the sensing capabilities of the vehicle (e.g. heavy rain, dense fog, snow, dirt); (iv) There are no overhead obstructions close to the vehicle; (d) The situation is unambiguous, i.e.: (i) The obstacle is stationary, unobstructed, clearly separated from other objects in the driving direction; (ii) The lateral offset between the centreline of the obstacle and the centreline of the vehicle is not more than 0.2 m (iii) The direction of travel is straight with no curve, and the vehicle is
When conditions deviate from those listed in paragraph 5.1.5. (a) through (d), the ACPE system shall not deactivate or unreasonably switch the control strategy.

The manufacturer shall demonstrate that the ACPE system does not deactivate or unreasonably switch the control strategy when conditions deviate from those listed in paragraph 5.1.5. (a) through (d) in accordance with Annex 3 of this Regulation, however, if deemed justified, this demonstration may be followed by testing by the Technical Service in conditions deviating from those listed in paragraph 5.1.5. (a) through (d) or those in paragraph 6.

The Technical Service shall append the rationale for and the results of the verification testing in conditions deviating from those listed in paragraph 5.1.5. (a) through (d) or those in paragraph 6 to the test report.

When a collision is not prevented, the ACPE shall ensure the collision speed is no greater than 8 km/h higher than the vehicle speed at the point where the triggering conditions specified in paragraph 5.1.2. are met.

When a collision is not prevented, the ACPE shall ensure the collision speed is not greater than 70% of that speed the vehicle would have had in the same position and under the same circumstances but without any ACPE intervention.

The vehicles that do not exceed 8 km/h without ACPE in the test scenarios but for which a speed reduction of 30 per cent cannot be achieved due to a low engine power to test mass ratio shall have a speed reduction of at least 15 per cent.
While any intervention is occurring, the ACPE shall continue to limit the vehicle acceleration.
When the obstacle is no longer detected, or the driver has interrupted the function, the ACPE shall be permitted to end the intervention.
The Manufacturer shall declare the ACPE continuation conditions to the technical service.
The ACPE shall not be adversely affected by magnetic or electrical fields.
The ACPE shall demonstrate effectiveness by fulfilling the technical requirements and respecting the transitional provisions of the 06 or later series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 10.
The conformity with the safety aspects of electronic control systems shall be shown by meeting the requirements of Annex 3.
The ACPE shall inform the driver of its intervention in accordance with paragraph 5.4.2.
The ACPE shall provide a means for the driver to interrupt its intervention.
When any intentional action which indicates that the driver has recognised the situation occurs, the ACPE shall start the interruption of the intervention.
When the accelerator control application is maintained during an interruption, the system shall prevent a rapid increase of acceleration.

When the manufacturer undergoes the inspection of the safety concept as part of the assessment to Annex 3, the manufacturer shall document the fulfilment of the requirements in paragraph 5.1.11. to the Approval Authority.

While the inspection of the safety concept as part of the assessment to Annex 3 is conducted, the manufacturer shall demonstrate the fulfilment of the requirements in paragraph 5.1.11. to the Approval Authority.

When a vehicle is equipped with a means to manually deactivate the ACPE, the ACPE shall be automatically reinstated at the initiation of any new engine start (or run cycle, as relevant), except that this requirement does not apply when a new engine start (or run cycle, as relevant) is performed automatically, e.g., the operation of a stop/start system.
When a vehicle is equipped with a means to manually deactivate the ACPE, the ACPE shall give a deactivation warning at least at the time of deactivation.

Where a vehicle is equipped with a long term deactivation means to manually deactivate the ACPE, the system shall provide information to the driver by either (a), (b) or (c): (a) A constant optical warning signal shall inform the driver that the ACPE has been deactivated. The yellow warning signal specified in paragraph 5.4.3. may be used for this purpose; (b) The driver shall be periodically informed that the ACPE has been deactivated. In this case this information shall be given for a minimum of 10 seconds or until driver confirmation. This information shall be given at least either every 7 days or every 10 engine starts (or run cycles, as relevant), not counting when a new engine start (or run cycle, as relevant) is performed automatically, e.g. the operation of a stop/start system. This information shall be distinct from the failure warning signal specified in paragraph 5.4.3.; or (c) If deactivation is only for one direction of operation (forward or rearwards), as an alternative to (a) or (b), a constant optical warning shall be given when the corresponding driving direction is selected for the first time following each initiation of the powertrain. The warning shall remain at least until the driving direction is changed.
The long-term deactivation process for the ACPE shall prevent deactivation with less than two deliberate actions.

Where the vehicle is equipped with a means to automatically deactivate the ACPE, for instance in situations such as carrying a bicycle rack or towing a trailer, the vehicle shall apply the following conditions as appropriate.
The vehicle manufacturer shall provide a list of situations and corresponding criteria where the ACPE is automatically deactivated to the technical service at the time of type-approval.
The list of situations and corresponding criteria where the ACPE is automatically deactivated shall be annexed to the test report.
When the conditions that led to the automatic deactivation are not present anymore, the ACPE shall be automatically reactivated.
When deactivation occurs, the system shall give a deactivation warning at least at the time of deactivation unless a failure warning is given as per paragraph 5.3.3.

While an Automated Driving System is in control of the vehicle (e.g. ALKS) and the risks associated with a pedal misapplication remain mitigated to the same degree as provided by ACPE, the ACPE shall be allowed to be suspended or its control strategies adapted without indication to the driver.

The manufacturer shall document the suspension of the ACPE or the adapted control strategies while an Automated Driving System is in control of the vehicle to the Approval Authority during the inspection of the safety concept as part of the assessment to Annex 3.

While an Automated Driving System is in control of the vehicle, the manufacturer shall demonstrate the suspension of the ACPE or the adapted control strategies to the Approval Authority during the inspection of the safety concept as part of the assessment to Annex 3.
If there is a failure in the ACPE that prevents the requirements of this Regulation being met, then the ACPE shall give a failure warning to the driver.
If there is a failure in the ACPE that prevents the requirements of this Regulation being met, then the ACPE shall provide a failure warning to the driver as specified in paragraph 5.4.3.
The ACPE shall not have an appreciable time interval between each self-check.

If an electrically detectable failure occurs, then the ACPE shall not delay in illuminating the warning signal, however, if the vehicle speed is greater than 10 km/h at the time a failure is detected, the warning signal may be suppressed until the next time the vehicle speed is below 10 km/h.

If a non-electrical failure condition (e.g. sensor blindness or sensor misalignment) is detected, then the system shall give a failure warning to the driver, unless a deactivation warning is given as per paragraph 5.2.3.1.3.
The optical warning signals shall be visible even by daylight.
The optical warning signals shall be easily verifiable by the driver from the driver's seat in their satisfactory condition.

When the engine start (or run, as relevant) switch is turned to the "on" (run) position or when the engine start (or run, as relevant) switch is in a position between the "on" (run) and "start" position that is designated by the manufacturer as a check position (initial system (power-on)), each ACPE optical warning signal shall be activated, except that this requirement does not apply to warning signals shown in a common space.
The vehicle shall give an intervention warning by an optical signal.

The vehicle system shall provide a haptic or acoustic signal to the driver in addition to the optical signal, unless such a signal is already being provided by another vehicle system comprising an object detection capability (e.g. parking distance warning).
The vehicle manufacturer shall provide a description of the intervention warning indication presented to the driver at the time of type-approval and record it in the test report.
The failure warning shall be given by a constant yellow optical signal.
When a Periodic Technical Inspection is performed, the ACPE shall allow the confirmation of its correct operational status by a visible observation of the failure warning signal status.

If any failure was present at the end of the previous engine start (or run, as relevant) cycle, then the failure warning signal shall remain illuminated following a “power-ON” and any bulb check, unless this failure is detected to be no longer present.
When the failure warning signal is in a common space, the common space shall be observed to be functional prior to the failure warning signal status check.

The manufacturer shall confidentially outline the means to protect against simple unauthorised modification of the operation of the failure warning signal at the time of type approval; alternatively, this protection requirement is fulfilled when a secondary means of checking the correct operational status of the ACPE is available.
The ambient temperature shall be between 0°C and 45°C.
The horizontal visibility range shall allow the target to be observed throughout the test.
While there is no wind liable to affect the results, the tests shall be performed.
The natural ambient illumination shall be homogeneous in the test area and in excess of 1000 lux.

When tests are conducted under deviating test conditions (suboptimal conditions, e.g. on a not dry surface; below the specified minimum ambient temperature) at the request of the manufacturer and with the agreement of the Technical Service, the system shall still meet the performance requirements.
The vehicle shall be measured for speed with an accuracy of +/- 0.1 km/h.
The vehicle shall have its position measured with an accuracy of +/- 0.03 m.
The accelerator control force (if applicable) shall be measured with an accuracy of +/- 1 N.
The accelerator control position shall be measured with an accuracy of +/- 1%, except that at the choice of the manufacturer, this measurement may be taken from the vehicle’s own position sensor.
The system shall record measurements at a frequency of at least 100 Hz.

The vehicle type approval documentation shall identify details of the pre-test condition strategy requested by the vehicle manufacturer, which may include driving the vehicle a maximum of 100 km on a mixture of urban and rural roads to initialise the sensor system and/or undergoing a sequence of brake activations to ensure the service brake system is bedded in.

The vehicle type approval documentation shall record details of the pre-test condition strategy requested by the vehicle manufacturer, which may include driving the vehicle a maximum of 100 km on a mixture of urban and rural roads to initialise the sensor system and/or undergoing a sequence of brake activations to ensure the service brake system is bedded in.
The vehicle shall be tested at the minimum mass (mass in running order with an additional mass of maximum 125 kg).

When the vehicle is tested, the vehicle shall be tested at the minimum mass (mass in running order with an additional mass of maximum 125 kg); however, if this is deemed justified, the technical service may test at any other mass up to the technically permissible maximum laden mass as defined by the manufacturer.
While the test procedure has begun, the vehicle shall have no alteration made to its mass.

The target used for the vehicle detection tests shall be a regular high-volume series production passenger car of Category M1 or alternatively a "soft target" representative of a passenger vehicle in terms of its identification characteristics applicable to the sensor system of the ACPE under test according to either ISO 19206-1:2018 or ISO 19206-3:2021 at the choice of the manufacturer.
For the accelerator control misapplication test, the lateral offset between the centreline of the target and the centreline of the vehicle shall be between 0.0 m and 0.2 m.

The accelerator control misapplication test procedure shall be performed with and without an expected ACPE intervention both in a forward and rearward direction and at least with the vehicle situated 1.0 m (+0.1 m tolerance) and 1.5 m (-0.1 m tolerance) from the target position at the start of the test (as detailed in Table 1).
The procedure for each accelerator control misapplication test shall be to position the vehicle at a distance to the target or speed measurement point as defined in Table 1.
The procedure for each accelerator control misapplication test shall hold the vehicle stationary and select the corresponding driving direction.

The procedure for each accelerator control misapplication test shall accelerate the vehicle, whilst maintaining the steering control in the neutral position, by operating the accelerator control in order to achieve the relevant triggering conditions (as outlined in paragraph 5.1.2.) before the vehicle reaches a speed of 0.5 km/h.
The procedure for each accelerator control misapplication test shall record the speed at the collision point (if applicable) or the speed at the respective speed measurement point.

When requested by the manufacturer, before any accelerator control misapplication test is started, the vehicle shall be allowed to be driven in the direction of the target for a distance of up to 20 m to the start position and/or the engine shall be allowed to be switched “off” and “on”.
When the vehicle type as defined in paragraph 2.2. is modified, the manufacturer shall notify the Type Approval Authority which approved the vehicle type.
The procedures concerning conformity of production shall comply with those set out in the 1958 Agreement, Schedule 1 (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3).
The procedures concerning conformity of production shall meet the following requirements: [the requirements that follow in the regulation].
The vehicle approved pursuant to this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements of paragraph 5. above.
